provenance.instrument: Warwick Township (Lancaster County) Code Chapter 340 Zoning (Warwick Township Zoning Ordinance of 1993, Ord. No. 159, 8-30-1993, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 code date 2025-02-19 (breadcrumb). New Laws on 2026-11-26 for Chapter 340: Ord. No. 306 (2026-04-15), Ord. No. 307 (2026-07-15) and Ord. No. 308 (undated rezoning), all read on 2026-11-26. None touches a dwelling use.
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 breadcrumb 'Code 2025-02-19'. Ord. No. 306 and 307 (2026) are listed as New Laws, not yet in the code text.
provenance.code_caution: Not yet in the online code, read from the New Laws PDFs: Ord. No. 306 (2026-04-15) adds drive-through fast-food restaurants as a conditional use in LC (340-16.1D(4), 340-66). Ord. No. 307 (2026-07-15) creates a Quarry Support Overlay Zone (340-20.1) on two parcels on Erbs Quarry Road and adds a TDR rule (340-45G(1)(d)). Ord. No. 308 rezones part of the former Weiser tract from CC to I-2. None changes the rules below.
checks: ECHO housing is a special exception only in the Agricultural (A) Zone: a portable elder cottage of at most 900 sq ft (340-11C(1), 340-67)
At least one occupant is 50 or older, handicapped or disabled, and related to the occupants of the house by blood, marriage or adoption. At most two people (340-67C, D)
The cottage connects to the house's sewage, water and other utilities. No separate systems. With on-site systems, evidence that they can serve both (340-67E)
Side or rear yard only, meeting the principal side and rear setbacks. Total building coverage within the zone maximum. One extra all-weather parking space (340-67B, F, G)
Temporary zoning permit reviewed every 12 months with a fee. The cottage is removed within three months after no qualifying person lives in it (340-67H, I)

In the A Zone, agriculture including one single-family detached dwelling on the site is permitted by right (340-11B(1)). A single-family detached dwelling that is not part of a farm is a conditional use, one per 20 acres of the 1985 parent tract. Lot 1 to 2 acres, or 15,000 sq ft with public sewer and water (340-11D(1), E(2), F(2))

Inside an approved Village Overlay (VO) development on R-2 land, 'Accessory building apartments with no more than one dwelling unit' are listed as a conditional use (340-23E(9)), while the lot table note says an accessory building apartment 'is permitted by special exception' (340-23J(1) note 4). Conflicting text, ask. Both refer to the criteria of 340-64, which is now conservation cluster developments. The matching criteria are in 340-65 (owner-occupied house, 10,000 sq ft lot, 4 parking spaces)

In a VO development an accessory building may be up to two stories when it holds an accessory apartment (15 ft otherwise). Accessory buildings 10 ft from the rear line and 6 ft from side lines, none in the front yard. Public sewer and public water throughout (340-23J(1) note 2, J(3)(a), N(1))

Temporary farm employee housing: one mobile home per farm for farm workers and their families, in the rear yard of the farm dwelling, by special exception in the A Zone. Occupied at least 120 days a year by a farm employee, or removed within 120 days (340-101)

Other paths: two-family conversion of a house of at least 3,000 sq ft that existed in 1993 (A and RE, special exception), conversion apartment in an existing house (MU and LC, conditional use), conversion of an accessory building of an owner-occupied house into one dwelling (VO overlay, special exception), and historic conversion apartments (A, C, RE, MU by special exception, LC and VO by conditional use) (340-103, 340-65, 340-61)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Warwick Township (Lancaster County) Zoning Officer. Read on eCode360 (WA2488) in a browser, one page at a time, on 2026-11-14. eCode360 WA1313 'Township of Warwick' is Warwick Township in Bucks County and was not used. Code search (all content) for 'accessory dwelling', 'accessory apartment', 'in-law', ECHO, granny, 'family dwelling', relative, caretaker, 'housekeeping unit', 'guest house', 'accessory unit', 'living quarters' and conversion found 340-65 and 340-103. The table of contents shows ECHO housing (340-67), conversion of historic structures (340-61) and temporary farm employee housing (340-101). Read: 340-11 (A Zone), 340-61, 340-65, 340-67, 340-103. Fix round 2026-11-14: read 340-23 (VO) in full, 340-101, and the Article IV contents (340-64 is now conservation cluster developments). Not read: the other zone use lists and tables (RE, C, R-1, R-2, R-3, MU, LC, CC, I-1, I-2, Q), definitions (340-10), accessory uses (340-25), parking (340-35), 340-14 and 340-121. Second review, 2026-11-26: Ord. No. 306, 307 and 308 read in full. The whole of Chapter 340 was read in one print view and searched by section for ECHO, apartment, accessory dwelling, in-law, elder cottage, two-family, duplex, conversion, caretaker, tenant house and farm employee: the listings are 340-11 (ECHO, farm employee housing, two-family conversions), 340-12 RE and 340-15 R-2 (two-family conversions), 340-12, 340-13, 340-16, 340-16.1 (historic conversions), 340-16 MU and 340-16.1 LC (conversion apartments), 340-23 VO, and duplexes by right in R-2, R-3 and VO. New finding fixed: R-2 lists two-family conversions as a special exception (340-15C(6)) though 340-103 names only A and RE (shown as disputed). Left for a later check: the VO accessory building apartment path (conditional use in 340-23E(9), special exception in note 4 of the lot table) and its stale 340-64 reference; the tool cannot key a status on the VO overlay, so R-2 keeps it as an alternative. Pass 30 (2026-11-26): adu.status_by_overlay gives an R-2 lot in the VO overlay the conditional use status, and the listing names the accessory building forms (detached new, garage conversion, over garage) and its owner rule.

term.note: The specific criteria call the unit an 'elder cottage'.

status.note: Special exception in the A Zone, for a relative who is 50 or older, handicapped or disabled. Portable and temporary.

scope_districts.note: 'Within the (A) Zone, ECHO housing is permitted by special exception.'

status_outside.note: No other zone lists ECHO housing in the sections read. The RE, C, R-1, R-2, R-3, MU, LC, CC, I-1, I-2 and Q use lists were not read. Inside an approved Village Overlay development on R-2 land the status differs (340-23E(9)).

value.note: Inside an approved Village Overlay development an accessory building apartment with no more than one dwelling unit is listed as a conditional use. Note 4 of the lot table and 340-65 say special exception, so the path is not settled

path.note: Zoning Hearing Board special exception, then a temporary zoning permit renewed every 12 months.

fallback_path.note: Relief from a zone rule is a variance from the Zoning Hearing Board.

value.name: Two-family conversion of a large existing house
value.conditions: A detached single-family dwelling that existed on the effective date of the chapter and then had at least 3,000 sq ft may become two dwelling units. Approved water and sewage, no extensions or outside changes, escape from upper floors, 4 off-street parking spaces, land development approval if required.

requires.condition: The house existed on the effective date of the chapter (adopted 8-30-1993)
The house had at least 3,000 sq ft on that date

value.note: The chapter was adopted 8-30-1993 (Ord. No. 159). Its effective date is read as that date, a reading to confirm with the Zoning Officer.

disputed_districts.note: The R-2 special exception list names 'Two-family conversions. (See § 340-103.)', but 340-103 opens 'Within the (A) and (RE) Zones'

value.name: Conversion apartment in an existing house
value.conditions: Only one apartment added within a single-family detached dwelling that existed on the effective date of the chapter. Lot at least 10,000 sq ft. Approved water and sewage. No outside change altering the residential look. At least 4 off-street parking spaces on the site. Upper-story unit with its own exterior escape.

requires.condition: The house existed on the effective date of the chapter

value.note: The effective date of the chapter is read as its adoption date, 8-30-1993 (Ord. No. 159). Confirm with the Zoning Officer.

value.name: Accessory building apartment in a Village Overlay development
value.conditions: No more than one dwelling unit, in an accessory building of an owner-occupied single-family detached dwelling. Lot at least 10,000 sq ft. Approved water and sewage (public sewer and water throughout a VO development). No outside change altering the residential look. At least 4 off-street parking spaces on the site. The accessory building may be up to two stories with an apartment (15 ft otherwise). Accessory buildings 10 ft from the rear line and 6 ft from side lines, none in the front yard.
value.note: Conflicting text, ask. 340-23E(9) lists 'Accessory building apartments with no more than one dwelling unit' as a conditional use. Note 4 of the lot table says 'an accessory building apartment is permitted by special exception', and 340-65 says the conversion of an accessory building in the VO Zone is by special exception. The cross-reference to 340-64 now points to conservation cluster developments, so the 340-65 criteria are read as the ones that apply. Only inside an approved Village Overlay development on R-2 land.

disputed_path.note: Note 4 of the lot table says 'an accessory building apartment is permitted by special exception', and 340-65 says the conversion of an accessory building in the VO Zone is by special exception

value.name: Temporary farm employee housing (one mobile home per farm)
value.conditions: For farm workers and their families employed by the farm owner, while the employee works the owner's land. In the rear yard of the farm dwelling, meeting the single-family setbacks. Anchored on a mobile home stand with a 6 inch concrete slab and utility connections. Occupied at least 120 days a year by a person employed on the farm, or removed within 120 days.

requires.condition: The lot is a farm and the occupant is employed by the farm owner

value.name: Historic conversion apartment
value.conditions: Only within historic structures. Each unit at least 400 sq ft of habitable floor area, outside changes complement the residential character, escape from upper and lower floors, 3 off-street parking spaces per unit, approved water and sewage. Conditional use in LC and VO.

requires.condition: The building is a historic structure as defined in the chapter

building_types.note: The cottage serves a principal dwelling on an agricultural lot.

historic_bypass.note: No historic path for ECHO housing.

value.condition: At least one occupant is at least 50 years old, handicapped or disabled, and related to the occupants of the house by blood, marriage or adoption. At most two people.
Physically connected to the house's sewage, water and other utility systems. No separate systems. With on-site systems, evidence they can serve both, Sewage Enforcement Officer review.
Portable construction. In the side or rear yard only, meeting the principal side and rear setbacks. Building coverage of house, accessory structures and cottage within the zone maximum.
Temporary zoning permit reviewed every 12 months with a fee. Removed within three months after it is no longer occupied by a qualifying person.

types_allowed.note: 'The elder cottage shall be of portable construction.'

max_sqft.note: 'May not exceed 900 square feet of floor area.'

district_yards_bind_accessory.note: 'Shall adhere to all side and rear yard setback requirements for principal uses.' A Zone house setbacks: side 15 ft each, rear 35 ft.

max_height_ft.note: Residential accessory uses on a parcel whose house was established on or after 11-13-1985: 20 ft. Pre-1985 parcels use the R-1 accessory figures (340-14, not read). 340-67 sets no height.

occupancy.value: At most two people. At least one is 50 or older, handicapped or disabled, and related to the occupants of the house by blood, marriage or adoption.

spaces_required.note: 'A minimum of one all-weather, off-street parking space ... in addition to that required for the principal dwelling.'

new_connection_required.note: 'No separate utility systems or connections shall be constructed or used.'

min_lot_sqft.note: With public sewer and public water. One acre otherwise, and at most two acres for a single-family dwelling. Width 100 ft at the setback line. A dwelling is a conditional use limited to one per 20 acres of the parent tract (340-11D(1), E(2)).

setback_side_ft.note: 15 ft each, 30 ft total, for a house built on or after 11-13-1985. Older houses use the R-1 figures (340-14, not read).

max_building_coverage.note: Lot coverage 20% for a house built on or after 11-13-1985.

accessory_setback_side_ft.note: Residential accessory uses, post-1985 house. An elder cottage takes the principal side setback, also 15 ft (340-67G).

value.when: Without public sewer and public water

utility_rows.note: 'Minimum lot area shall be one acre ... may be reduced to 15,000 square feet if both public sewer and public water are utilized.'
